3663244.background: Brasília (DF) is a strong Bolsonaro bastion: Jair Bolsonaro took about 59% there in the 2022 first round. Jailed Jair endorsed his son, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, as the right's 2026 candidate against Lula. Other right candidates (e.g., Caiado, Zema, Ratinho Jr) may split the conservative vote.

actors.name: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL)
actors.public: Bolsonaro family heir and PL nominee; inherits the family brand and PL machine; weaker personal charisma than his father, carries rachadinha scandal baggage.
actors.private: Needs to consolidate the right early; Brasília civil-servant and evangelical base is his safest ground; fears a rival right candidate eroding him.

actors.name: Lula (PT)
actors.public: Incumbent seeking reelection; won about 37% in DF in 2022; strong with lower-income satellite cities.
actors.private: Treats DF as a loss to minimize; focuses resources on Southeast and Northeast.

actors.name: Federal District electorate
actors.public: Affluent, public-sector heavy, strongly anti-PT in recent cycles; also pivotal evangelical bloc.
actors.private: Some center-right voters may prefer a less polarizing non-Bolsonaro conservative if one looks viable.

events.name: Flávio candidacy blocked or replaced (court, health, family decision)
Another right-wing candidate surges nationally above Flávio

3663284.background: Espírito Santo leaned right in 2022 (Bolsonaro about 52% first round vs Lula about 40%). Flávio Bolsonaro is the Bolsonaro-endorsed nominee against Lula; centrist and center-right alternatives exist. Governor Casagrande (PSB) is a Lula ally but the state's presidential vote is conservative-leaning.

actors.name: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL)
actors.public: Bolsonaro family candidate with PL backing and evangelical support, strong in Southeast interior.
actors.private: Must hold Jair's 2022 coalition; vulnerable if voters see him as weaker heir.

actors.name: Lula (PT)
actors.public: Incumbent; won about 40% in ES in 2022 with PSB allies' support.
actors.private: Hopes economic gains (income tax exemption, minimum wage) narrow the gap; ES not a priority.

actors.name: Center-right rivals (Zema, Caiado, Ratinho Jr or others)
actors.public: Pitch themselves as non-radical anti-Lula options.
actors.private: Aim to reach second round; may peel off moderate Bolsonaro voters.

events.name: A rival right candidate overtakes Flávio nationally

3663332.background: Goiás is agribusiness-heavy and pro-Bolsonaro (about 58% for Jair in 2022 first round). Governor Ronaldo Caiado sought the presidency himself; if he runs, he is a strong favorite-son competitor to Flávio Bolsonaro in his home state.

actors.name: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL)
actors.public: Bolsonaro-endorsed nominee; PL and agribusiness ties.
actors.private: Wants to absorb Caiado's voters; a Caiado home-state win would embarrass him.

actors.name: Ronaldo Caiado
actors.public: Popular two-term Goiás governor, high approval, declared presidential ambition, tough-on-crime brand.
actors.private: May withdraw or form an alliance if nationally stuck in single digits; home-state result is key to his relevance.

actors.name: Lula (PT)
actors.public: Incumbent; about 35-40% in Goiás in 2022.
actors.private: Benefits from right fragmentation but unlikely to top Goiás.

events.name: Caiado is on the ballot as presidential candidate

3663414.background: Minas Gerais is Brazil's bellwether; Lula won it narrowly in 2022 (about 48% vs 44% first round). Former governor Romeu Zema (Novo) is a presidential candidate with home-state strength, competing with Flávio Bolsonaro for right-wing votes.

actors.name: Lula (PT)
actors.public: Incumbent; won MG in both 2022 rounds; strong in north Minas and Jequitinhonha valley.
actors.private: Sees MG as must-win; will campaign heavily there; vulnerable to economic discontent in Triângulo/south.

actors.name: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL)
actors.public: Bolsonaro nominee; inherits Jair's strong Minas south/Triângulo base.
actors.private: Needs Zema voters; fragmentation helps Lula top the first round.

actors.name: Romeu Zema (Novo)
actors.public: Two-term governor, popular in MG, liberal-conservative pitch.
actors.private: May drop out if nationally weak; home-state vote share defines his future.

events.name: Significant shift in Lula approval (+/-5 pts)

3663534.background: Pará voted for Lula in 2022 (about 52% first round vs 41% Bolsonaro). Governor Helder Barbalho (MDB) is a Lula ally; Belém hosted COP30 in 2025. Flávio Bolsonaro leads the right.

actors.name: Lula (PT)
actors.public: Incumbent with Northern/Northeastern social-program base; allied with Barbalho family.
actors.private: Expects Pará win; relies on Bolsa Família and Barbalho machine.

actors.name: Helder Barbalho / MDB Pará
actors.public: Powerful governor machine; supported Lula in 2022.
actors.private: Loyalty transactional; MDB nationally split, may hedge if Lula weakens.

actors.name: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL)
actors.public: Strong in agribusiness/mining south-east Pará.
actors.private: Aims to narrow margin rather than win the state.

3663584.background: Paraíba is a Northeastern PT stronghold; Lula took about 64% there in the 2022 first round. Flávio Bolsonaro is the right's main candidate.

actors.name: Lula (PT)
actors.public: Northeastern native, incumbent, social programs; dominant regional base.
actors.private: Counts on huge Northeast margins to offset South/Center-West.

actors.name: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL)
actors.public: Bolsonaro nominee, evangelical outreach.
actors.private: Seeks to cut Lula's margin, not win.

actors.name: Paraíba governing coalition (João Azevêdo, PSB)
actors.public: Allied with Lula.
actors.private: Will mobilize for Lula alongside own state races.

3663636.background: Pernambuco is Lula's home state; he took about 65% there in the 2022 first round. Governor Raquel Lyra (PSD) is center-right; Recife mayor João Campos (PSB) allied with Lula.

actors.name: Lula (PT)
actors.public: Native son; incumbent; dominant in the Northeast.
actors.private: Expects overwhelming win; uses state as margin reservoir.

actors.name: João Campos (PSB)
actors.public: Popular Recife mayor, Lula ally, likely governor candidate.
actors.private: His own race aligns him strongly with Lula's campaign.

actors.name: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL)
actors.public: Bolsonaro nominee.
actors.private: Aims only to limit losses.

3663834.background: Rondônia is one of Bolsonaro's strongest states (about 65% in the 2022 first round). Agribusiness and frontier economy; Flávio Bolsonaro is the Bolsonaro-endorsed candidate.

actors.name: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL)
actors.public: Bolsonaro nominee; inherits strong agribusiness/evangelical support.
actors.private: Expects comfortable win; only risk is another right candidate splitting votes.

actors.name: Lula (PT)
actors.public: Incumbent; around 30% in 2022.
actors.private: Not competing seriously in Rondônia.

actors.name: Other right candidates (Caiado, Zema, Ratinho Jr)
actors.public: Court the same agribusiness electorate.
actors.private: Unlikely to overtake the Bolsonaro brand in the North frontier.

3663914.background: Rio Grande do Sul leaned Bolsonaro in 2022 (about 49% vs 43% for Lula in first round). Porto Alegre and the metro lean left; interior strongly right. Governor Eduardo Leite (PSD) had presidential ambitions; Flávio Bolsonaro is the right's main nominee.

actors.name: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL)
actors.public: Bolsonaro nominee; strong in gaúcho interior/agribusiness.
actors.private: Must hold Jair's margin despite potential competition from Leite or Ratinho Jr.

actors.name: Lula (PT)
actors.public: Incumbent; delivered federal aid after 2024 floods.
actors.private: Hopes flood-relief credit and metro vote narrow the gap.

actors.name: Eduardo Leite / PSD candidate
actors.public: Moderate center-right governor; may run or back PSD nominee.
actors.private: A Leite run would split right-leaning moderates in RS.

events.name: A gaúcho or southern center-right candidate on presidential ballot (Leite/Ratinho Jr)

3664068.background: Tocantins leaned to Bolsonaro in 2022 but closer than neighbors (roughly 51% vs 45%). Agribusiness frontier state with Northeastern-style poorer areas. Flávio Bolsonaro is the right's candidate against Lula.

actors.name: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL)
actors.public: Bolsonaro nominee, agribusiness support.
actors.private: Needs to retain Jair's narrow edge; less personal pull than his father.

actors.name: Lula (PT)
actors.public: Incumbent; competitive in Tocantins through social programs.
actors.private: Sees state as reachable if right fragments.

actors.name: Ronaldo Caiado / other right candidates
actors.public: Caiado from neighboring Goiás has regional appeal.
actors.private: Could divert enough votes to let Lula top the plurality.

3669979.background: Trump designated cartels as terrorist organizations, struck alleged drug boats in the Caribbean/Pacific from September 2025 (maritime, excluded), and US forces seized Maduro in Venezuela in January 2026. Trump repeatedly threatened land strikes on cartels; Mexico's Sheinbaum rejects US unilateral action.

actors.name: Trump administration / Pentagon
actors.public: Declares armed conflict with narco-terrorists; repeatedly promises strikes 'on land'; has shown willingness to act in Venezuela.
actors.private: Wants visible wins before midterms; prefers strikes with low US casualty risk; deterred somewhat by Mexico trade/USMCA stakes.

actors.name: Claudia Sheinbaum (Mexico)
actors.public: Red line against US troops/strikes on Mexican soil; cooperates on extraditions and fentanyl crackdowns.
actors.private: Would tolerate quiet intelligence cooperation; unilateral strike would trigger major crisis.

actors.name: Venezuela post-Maduro authorities / Colombia (Petro)
actors.public: Venezuela under heavy US pressure; Petro hostile to US strikes.
actors.private: Venezuelan interim leadership may permit or not resist US anti-drug actions on its soil.

events.name: US strike on land target in Venezuela/Colombia/Mexico announced
Joint US-host raid publicly confirmed with US personnel
Major cartel attack on US citizens prompting retaliation

3698019.background: Brazilian TV networks (Band traditionally first, then Globo, SBT, CNN etc.) hold presidential debates from August until days before the first round. Flávio Bolsonaro is the PL nominee; Jair skipped some 2018 debates (after stabbing) but attended in 2022.

actors.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
actors.public: Experienced senator and media-facing; campaign needs exposure to establish himself as main anti-Lula option.
actors.private: May skip select debates if leading or to avoid attacks, but unlikely to skip all.

actors.name: Lula
actors.public: Attended debates in 2022; may skip some as incumbent.
actors.private: His absence does not block debates featuring other candidates.

actors.name: TV networks (Band, Globo, SBT, Record, CNN Brasil)
actors.public: Legally must invite candidates of parties with sufficient congressional seats; PL qualifies.
actors.private: Strong commercial interest in hosting multiple debates.

events.name: Flávio candidacy replaced or blocked before debates

3701623.background: Karoline Leavitt has been White House Press Secretary since January 2025. She was expecting a child around May 2026, prompting speculation about leave or departure. Acting/interim appointments do not count.

actors.name: Karoline Leavitt
actors.public: Combative, loyal Trump spokesperson; highly visible.
actors.private: May take maternity leave or eye a congressional/media move; could plan exit after midterms rather than before.

actors.name: Donald Trump
actors.public: Praises Leavitt; values loyalty and TV performance.
actors.private: Prefers stability before midterms; would quickly pick a loyalist replacement if she leaves.

actors.name: White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles / comms team
actors.public: Manage staffing.
actors.private: Would likely name a deputy (e.g., Harrison Fields/others) acting rather than permanent during short leave.

3708435.background: After 2025, Republicans hold 26 governorships and Democrats 24 (Democrats flipped Virginia, held New Jersey). 36 governorships are contested November 2026; a midterm under a Republican president historically favors the out-party.

actors.name: Democratic Governors Association
actors.public: Targets open seats in Georgia, Arizona hold, Nevada, Iowa, Ohio, New Hampshire, Wisconsin hold, Michigan hold.
actors.private: Needs net +2 for majority; must defend Arizona, Michigan, Wisconsin, Kansas open seat.

actors.name: Republican Governors Association
actors.public: Defends Georgia, Nevada, Iowa, Ohio; targets Kansas, Arizona, Michigan, Wisconsin.
actors.private: Expects losses given midterm environment; aims to limit them.

actors.name: National electorate
actors.public: Trump approval roughly low-40s; generic ballot favors Democrats.
actors.private: Midterm penalty typical; independents in Michigan (Duggan) complicate counts.

events.name: National environment swings toward GOP (generic ballot narrows to tie)

3728838.background: Les Républicains' Senate group (largest, around 130 members) dominates the right-of-center Senate majority. The September 2026 election renews 178 seats (série 2) via indirect vote by local electors, following the March 2026 municipal elections.

actors.name: Groupe LR (Mathieu Darnaud, Bruno Retailleau)
actors.public: Largest group; strong rural/local elected base; Retailleau party leader.
actors.private: Aims to hold or gain seats; recruitment of apparentés/rattachés after vote can shift count by several.

actors.name: Grands électeurs (municipal councillors)
actors.public: Electorate shaped by 2026 municipals, where LR and allies held up well locally.
actors.private: Personal votes for incumbents dominate; slow-moving.

actors.name: Centrist Union / Horizons / RN
actors.public: Compete for center-right seats; RN seeks more seats.
actors.private: Some senators may switch between LR and centrist groups post-election.

events.name: Defections/realignments between LR and centrist groups after election
Dissolution or national political crisis shifting dynamics

3729337.background: Georgia 2026: Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff seeks reelection; governor seat is open (Kemp term-limited). Republican nominees from primaries (e.g., Burt Jones for governor). Democrats hold the Senate seat; governor candidates include Keisha Lance Bottoms. 50% runoff rule applies.

actors.name: Jon Ossoff
actors.public: Incumbent, huge fundraising, favored in a Democratic-leaning midterm.
actors.private: Will run independent of national party branding; vulnerable to runoff if third parties draw votes.

actors.name: Democratic gubernatorial nominee
actors.public: Faces open-seat race in a state Republicans have held since 2003.
actors.private: Needs high Black turnout and suburban swing; weaker funding than Ossoff.

actors.name: Georgia Republicans (Burt Jones/Kemp network)
actors.public: Trump-endorsed governor candidate; Kemp's machine strong.
actors.private: Prioritize governorship hold; Senate nominee may be weaker.

events.name: Either race goes to December runoff

3729379.background: Minnesota 2026: governor race (Tim Walz initially sought a third term but withdrew in January 2026 amid fraud-scandal fallout; Amy Klobuchar entered) and open Senate seat (Tina Smith retiring; Peggy Flanagan vs Angie Craig in DFL primary). Minnesota last elected a Republican statewide in 2006.

actors.name: DFL (Democratic-Farmer-Labor) party
actors.public: Holds all statewide offices; strong midterm environment.
actors.private: Feeding-program fraud scandals are a liability; consolidating behind strong nominees.

actors.name: Minnesota Republicans
actors.public: Hope to exploit fraud scandal; candidates include Lisa Demuth, Royce White-type populists for Senate.
actors.private: Lack top-tier statewide candidates; hope for open-seat upset.

actors.name: Minnesota electorate
actors.public: Lean-blue; Harris won by about 4 in 2024.
actors.private: Suburban swing voters drive margin.

3741437.background: Ontario by-election in Scarborough Southwest, a seat held by the NDP's Doly Begum until she left (crossed to the federal Liberals in 2025). Doug Ford's PCs, Bonnie Crombie's Liberals and the NDP compete; Fatima Shaban is a candidate (party uncertain to me).

actors.name: Ontario NDP (Marit Stiles)
actors.public: Held the riding since 2018 with Begum.
actors.private: Personal vote of Begum may not transfer; must defend Official Opposition status.

actors.name: Ontario Liberals
actors.public: Strong federally in Scarborough; rebuilding provincially.
actors.private: See by-election as a pickup chance.

actors.name: Ontario PCs (Doug Ford)
actors.public: Comfortable majority; competitive in Scarborough since 2018.
actors.private: By-elections low priority; could win on split opposition vote.

actors.name: Scarborough Southwest voters
actors.public: Diverse, working/middle class; low by-election turnout.
actors.private: Ethnic community organizing heavily matters in low-turnout contests.

events.name: Province-wide scandal hitting a contesting party

3748337.background: Berlin state election 20 Sept 2026. In 2023 CDU won 28.2% and Kai Wegner became mayor with SPD. 2025-26 polls put CDU around 22-26%, with Linke surging, AfD around 14-16%, Greens around 13-15%, SPD around 11-14%.

actors.name: CDU Berlin (Kai Wegner)
actors.public: Incumbent mayor; campaign on security, administration.
actors.private: Hurt by federal Merz government unpopularity and housing issue; fears losing first place to Linke.

actors.name: Die Linke Berlin
actors.public: Surging on housing/rent issues after 2025 federal comeback.
actors.private: Aims for first place and red-red-green majority.

actors.name: Berlin electorate
actors.public: Polarized East/West, young urban left vote.
actors.private: Late swings common in city-state elections.

events.name: Major security incident in Berlin raising CDU/AfD salience

3748343.background: Berlin election 20 Sept 2026. Linke won 12.2% in 2023 but surged after its 2025 federal result (it topped Berlin party-list vote at ~19.9%). Polls in 2026 show Linke around 15-20%, competing with CDU for first place.

actors.name: Die Linke Berlin (Elif Eralp as lead candidate)
actors.public: Rent/housing campaign, strong young voter base, membership boom.
actors.private: Needs to beat CDU; risk of overestimated poll momentum.

actors.name: Greens Berlin
actors.public: Compete for same urban progressive voters.
actors.private: Losing voters to Linke.

actors.name: CDU Berlin (Wegner)
actors.public: Frames race as CDU vs Linke.
actors.private: Polarization may mobilize both sides.

3748347.background: Berlin election 20 Sept 2026. AfD got 9.1% in 2023 and about 15% in Berlin in the 2025 federal election. 2026 polls show AfD around 14-17%, strong in eastern outer districts.

actors.name: AfD Berlin
actors.public: Strong in Marzahn-Hellersdorf, Lichtenberg, Treptow-Köpenick; national high polling.
actors.private: Berlin is a ceiling-limited city for AfD due to large urban progressive electorate.

actors.name: CDU Berlin
actors.public: Competes for law-and-order voters.
actors.private: Tough-on-migration messaging aims to contain AfD.

actors.name: Berlin electorate
actors.public: Western districts largely immune to AfD.
actors.private: Turnout mobilization against AfD likely.

3748348.background: Berlin election 20 Sept 2026. Greens won 18.4% in 2023; polls in 2025-26 show them around 13-16%, losing urban voters to Linke. Lead candidate Bettina Jarasch / Werner Graf leadership.

actors.name: Greens Berlin
actors.public: Inner-city base (Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg, Mitte, Pankow).
actors.private: Squeezed by Linke on the left; risk of falling to 4th place.

actors.name: Die Linke Berlin
actors.public: Taking young progressive voters.
actors.private: Wants to become dominant left party.

actors.name: Berlin electorate
actors.public: Young progressive cohort mobile between Greens and Linke.
actors.private: Tactical voting may follow polls.

3748352.background: Berlin election 20 Sept 2026. SPD won 18.4% in 2023 (junior partner to CDU since). Polls 2025-26 show SPD around 11-15%, historic lows; lead candidate Steffen Krach.

actors.name: SPD Berlin (Steffen Krach)
actors.public: Junior coalition partner; weak brand, internal divisions.
actors.private: Fears single digits; hopes Krach's profile and governing record stabilize.

actors.name: Die Linke Berlin
actors.public: Draws left-leaning former SPD voters.
actors.private: Benefits from SPD weakness.

actors.name: Federal SPD in Merz coalition
actors.public: Unpopular national position.
actors.private: Federal drag on state party.

events.name: Late campaign boost from candidate debates

3748409.background: Saxony-Anhalt election 6 Sept 2026. AfD won 20.8% in 2021 but led 2025-26 polls at roughly 38-40%, with lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund. CDU (Sven Schulze replaced Haseloff as lead) around 26-27%.

actors.name: AfD Sachsen-Anhalt (Ulrich Siegmund)
actors.public: Polling first, aiming for absolute majority of seats; classified extremist by state intelligence.
actors.private: Needs near-40%+ and many small parties below 5% to govern alone.

actors.name: CDU Sachsen-Anhalt (Sven Schulze)
actors.public: Incumbent leading party; 'Brandmauer' against AfD.
actors.private: Hopes rally-around incumbent effect; may squeeze AfD in final weeks.

actors.name: Saxony-Anhalt electorate
actors.public: Highly dissatisfied, strong AfD protest vote.
actors.private: Anti-AfD tactical voting toward CDU possible.

3748412.background: Saxony-Anhalt election 6 Sept 2026. CDU won 37.1% in 2021 under Haseloff. In 2025-26 polls CDU is about 25-28% behind AfD near 39%. Sven Schulze succeeded Haseloff as minister-president/lead candidate.

actors.name: CDU Sachsen-Anhalt (Sven Schulze)
actors.public: Governing party, 'stop AfD' campaign.
actors.private: Needs tactical votes from SPD/Greens/Linke voters to stay first or close.

actors.name: AfD Sachsen-Anhalt
actors.public: Polling first.
actors.private: Polarization helps both AfD and CDU.

actors.name: Federal Merz government
actors.public: CDU-led coalition nationally.
actors.private: Unpopularity drags state CDU.

events.name: Strong late anti-AfD tactical swing to CDU

3748582.background: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern election 20 Sept 2026. AfD won 16.7% in 2021 but led 2025-26 polls at about 35-38%. SPD under Manuela Schwesig (39.6% in 2021) polls about 20-25%.

actors.name: AfD MV (Leif-Erik Holm)
actors.public: Polling first, seeking to govern.
actors.private: Needs fragmentation of others for majority.

actors.name: SPD MV (Manuela Schwesig)
actors.public: Popular incumbent; personal bonus.
actors.private: Aims to close gap via incumbency duel; Nord Stream 2 foundation baggage.

actors.name: MV electorate
actors.public: Dissatisfied east German voters.
actors.private: Late swing to Schwesig as in 2021 possible.

events.name: Late swing to Schwesig in duel framing

3748586.background: MV election 20 Sept 2026. SPD won 39.6% in 2021 under Manuela Schwesig, governs with Linke. 2025-26 polls: SPD about 19-25%, AfD 35-38%, CDU 12-14%, Linke ~10%, BSW 5-8%.

actors.name: SPD MV (Manuela Schwesig)
actors.public: Popular minister-president, strong campaigner; 2021 surged late.
actors.private: Needs duel framing against AfD to absorb tactical votes.

actors.name: AfD MV
actors.public: Polling first.
actors.private: Its strength motivates anti-AfD consolidation.

actors.name: Federal SPD
actors.public: Junior partner nationally.
actors.private: Federal unpopularity is a drag.

events.name: Major late tactical shift to SPD

3748590.background: MV election 20 Sept 2026. CDU won 13.3% in 2021; 2025-26 polls show CDU about 11-14%, squeezed between AfD and SPD's Schwesig duel.

actors.name: CDU MV (Daniel Peters)
actors.public: Opposition party; weak profile.
actors.private: Risks squeeze from tactical voting to SPD or AfD.

actors.name: SPD MV / AfD MV
actors.public: Dominate duel framing.
actors.private: Both drain CDU voters.

actors.name: Federal Merz government
actors.public: CDU-led.
actors.private: Unpopularity drags state CDU.

3748594.background: MV election 20 Sept 2026. Linke won 9.9% in 2021 and governs with SPD. After its 2025 federal revival, polls show Linke around 9-13% in MV.

actors.name: Die Linke MV
actors.public: Coalition partner; benefiting from national revival.
actors.private: Fears losing votes to SPD tactical consolidation and BSW.

actors.name: SPD MV (Schwesig)
actors.public: Coalition partner.
actors.private: Duel with AfD may draw Linke voters.

actors.name: BSW
actors.public: Competes for left-populist voters.
actors.private: Weakening nationally after 2025 failure.

events.name: Tactical voting shift from Linke to SPD

3748600.background: MV election 20 Sept 2026. BSW (Sahra Wagenknecht's party) narrowly missed Bundestag in 2025 (4.98%); it entered eastern Landtage in 2024. MV polls 2025-26 put BSW roughly 4-8%.

actors.name: BSW MV
actors.public: Peace/Russia-friendly, left-conservative pitch; weak local organization.
actors.private: Fighting for 5% threshold; internal splits and Wagenknecht's reduced role hurt.

actors.name: AfD MV
actors.public: Competes for protest voters.
actors.private: Absorbs BSW voters.

actors.name: Die Linke / SPD
actors.public: Compete for left voters.
actors.private: Linke revival drains BSW.
